summary: Candidates came from reading notes and scoring hand-written regexes by balanced accuracy vs label. The SAE-gradient proxy (F@g) was checked against sample logits. A generator built from hand-written lowercase bodies produced 60 texts per probe over six near-orthogonal binary factors (topic, pronoun, case, greeting, aside, sign-off). Each factor's effect was estimated by regressing F@g on the factors and dividing by the topic coefficient. True logits were then read on one-factor edits of one fixed body. A word/symbol scan across both probes looked for missed properties. Latents for the case cue were ranked by g times their case coefficient from a regression on the public corpus. The final set was the plain top 16, checked by ablation on sample notes.

phases.purpose: Read task layout, label balance and full example notes of each label for both probes
Score two rounds of hand-written property regexes by balanced accuracy vs label in each probe; flag near-perfect separators
Validate linear proxy: regress probe-0 sample logits on F@g (slope, R2)
Check that lowercase-style notes contain no uppercase letter; list greeting vocabulary for the generator
Build a template generator with six binary factors and nuisance coin-flips; regenerate with a searched design after the first one was too correlated
Regress F@g of 60 factorial texts per probe on factors; express each factor as a fraction of the topic coefficient with 0.3/0.15 flags
True-logit check on one fixed body: probe 0 2x2 topic x case, probe 1 baseline/case/greeting/topic
Data-driven unigram/symbol/structure scan for features near-perfectly separating labels in both probes
Per-latent regression on probe-1 factorial texts; rank latents by g*case-coef; greedy prefix predicted removal vs topic kept
Repeat the per-latent regression on the 192 corpus notes with regex-detected properties; greedy selection requiring positive contribution in both sources and topic kept >=0.88
Compare proxy vs true edit effects on the 8 checked texts; fit probe-1 sample amplification slope to bound reachable removal
Compare topic-filtered vs unfiltered top-16 by corpus case contribution; verify [A-Z] against first-letter case on corpus
Ablate the topic-filtered set, then the unfiltered top-16, on probe-1 sample notes; compare separation retained and accuracy
Corpus single-property case regression for both probe gradients as a probe-0 cross-check; assemble and submit

probe_query_use.purpose: Measure true case effect relative to topic effect for probe 0

per_probe.procedure: Case, pronoun, greeting, P.S. style and asides were all perfectly locked to the label in the sample. In the 60-text factorial, every non-topic factor's F@g regression coefficient stayed below 0.15 of the topic coefficient (largest was case). A true-logit 2x2 of topic x case on one fixed body gave a case effect about -0.03 of the topic effect. The cross-probe token scan found no further candidate. Later, a corpus regression of case alone gave a small total g*coef for probe 0 against its large topic effect. All of this together led to answering none.
per_probe.quote: Probe 0 shows all properties below 0.15 — suggesting no main cue. Let me check probe 1 now.

per_probe.procedure: The factorial F@g regression gave case at about 2x the topic coefficient and greeting as borderline. A true-logit check on one fixed body confirmed a large case effect (about 1.6x topic) and a small greeting effect, so case was taken as the only cue. Regex [A-Z] was chosen after checking that lowercase-style notes have no uppercase letters, in both the sample and the corpus. Latents were ranked by gradient times their case coefficient from a multi-property regression on the corpus. A topic-filtered greedy set was dropped for the plain top 16 by positive contribution, which captured more. Ablation on sample notes kept accuracy and reduced separation.
per_probe.quote: Including 11138 (pure top-16 by cap) gives better capture (0.81). Let me verify my regex detects capitalization robustly on the corpus, and confirm the final latent set.

decision_points.choice: Read example notes, then wrote regexes for pronoun, greeting case, P.S. case, asides, emoticons, hashtags, mottos, first-letter case, and sign-offs. Each was scored by balanced accuracy vs label. A later word/symbol unigram scan across both probes checked for missed properties.

decision_points.choice: A programmatic template generator using 3 hand-written lowercase bodies per topic with pronoun slots and six crossed binary factors (topic, pronoun, case, greeting, aside, sign-off), plus random nuisance extras. The design was searched over 6000 random balanced layouts to minimize factor correlation.
Regress the gradient x SAE latent-means proxy (F@g) of the factorial texts on factor indicators; dependence = factor coef / topic coef. Checked against true logits on one-factor edits.
Eight true-logit texts spent in one step, split 4+4: probe 0 got a topic x case 2x2; probe 1 got baseline, case flip, greeting flip and topic flip on one body.

decision_points.choice: Per-latent OLS of corpus latent means on five regex-detected properties. Score = probe-1 gradient x case coefficient. Took the top 16 with positive score, with no topic filter. Earlier variants (factorial-only greedy, positive-in-both with topic kept >=0.88, skip topic contribution >0.06) were dropped.

caveats: The generator bodies are abbreviated in the script, since the full texts are in the log. The step-60 ablation used the topic-filtered set from step 56, because that file had been overwritten, so the script passes that set. The step-62 ablation analysis re-read the same result with the correct key; the earlier summary had read the wrong field. Some output tables were truncated in the log (probe-1 round-1 scan rows, part of the top-latent lists), so the exact ranks past about 20 are not visible. Probe 0 sample latent means were used only for proxy calibration.
